newsitem.title: USA: Chevron says UK downstream sale most likely.
newsitem.headline: Chevron says UK downstream sale most likely.

text.p: Chevron Corp is still reviewing the options for its UK refining assets, but the company believes that a sale is the most likely option, a spokesman for Chevron said.
"We have always said that we do not continue to have a significant interest in the UK downstream," a company spokesman said.
A deal to merge its UK downstream assets with France's Elf Aquitaine fell through on Friday.
The Chevron spokesman said that options apart from a sale were either to break the unit up into smaller parts prior to a sale or radically downsize the operation.
The company said that the closure of the main UK downstream asset, the 115,000 barrel per day refinery at Milford Haven in Pembrokeshire, remained an option.
Apart from that, the company has distribution operations, terminals and 470 gasoline stations.
The deal to merge Elf and Chevron's UK downstream was dealt a blow earlier this year when Murphy Oil Corp withdrew from what had been planned as a three-way deal.
The deal had originally been intended to save the three companies 50 million sterling a year.
Chevron said that it is still in talks to sell its 50 percent interest in the Pembroke Cracking Co to Texaco Inc, its partner in the venture.
